2027-03-23.title: Tuesday of Holy Week
readings: I will give you as a light to the nations, that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth (Second Song of the Servant)
I will sing of your salvation
One of you will betray me. Before the cock crows, you will have denied me three times
2027-03-23.alt: Holy Week. Lent continues until the evening Mass of the Lord's Supper on Thursday. No Gloria, no Alleluia. Liturgical colour: violet. The memorial of St Turibius of Mogrovejo, bishop, is not celebrated this year, because no memorial is kept during Holy Week.
2027-03-23.verse: I will give you as a light to the nations, that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth.
theo: Today the second Song of the Servant lets the Servant himself speak. “The LORD called me before I was born, while I was in my mother's womb he named me.” God has shaped him like a sharp sword and a polished arrow, hidden in his quiver until the right moment. Yet the Servant also knows the taste of failure: “I have labored in vain, I have spent my strength for nothing and vanity; yet surely my cause is with the LORD.” God's answer is astonishing. Instead of reducing the mission, he enlarges it: “It is too light a thing that you should be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob… I will give you as a light to the nations, that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth.” On Tuesday of Holy Week we hear this as the prayer of Jesus. To human eyes his work in Jerusalem is collapsing; one of the Twelve is about to sell him, another will deny him, the rest will run. Yet through that apparent failure the light will reach the whole world, even to the shores of India. The Psalm is the prayer of one who has trusted God from the womb: “Upon you I have leaned from my birth.”

The Gospel takes us into the Upper Room. Jesus has just washed the feet of the disciples, and now he is “troubled in spirit” and says: “Very truly, I tell you, one of you will betray me.” The disciples look at one another. The beloved disciple, reclining next to Jesus, asks: “Lord, who is it?” Jesus dips a piece of bread and gives it to Judas. In the East, to give a morsel from the dish to a guest was a sign of honour and friendship. Even at this moment Jesus offers Judas love. But Judas takes the bread and goes out. St John adds four words that fall like a stone: “And it was night.” Not only the night outside, but the night of a heart that refuses the light. And yet Jesus says: “Now the Son of Man has been glorified.” The hour of betrayal is also the hour of glory, because love is about to be shown to the end.

Then Peter speaks with all his warm, impulsive heart: “Lord, why can I not follow you now? I will lay down my life for you.” Jesus answers gently and truly: “Will you lay down your life for me? Very truly, I tell you, before the cock crows, you will have denied me three times.” Two disciples fail the Lord on the same night. The difference between them is not the size of their sin, but what they do afterwards. Judas goes out into the night and despairs. Peter will meet the gaze of Jesus, weep bitterly, and return (Luke 22:61–62). Jesus had said, “Where I am going, you cannot follow me now; but you will follow afterward”; and Peter did follow, to Rome and to his own cross. Holy Week is the time to be honest about our betrayals and denials, and to choose Peter's tears instead of Judas's night. No one is too far gone for the mercy of the One who gave the morsel even to his betrayer.
conn: Isaiah 49:1–6. Paul and Barnabas quote verse 6 to explain their mission to the Gentiles (Acts 13:47): the Servant's light passes to the Church.
At a festive meal guests lay on cushions around a low table, leaning on the left elbow. The beloved disciple, at the right of Jesus, could lean back against his chest to ask him privately.
The host's gift of a piece of bread dipped in the dish was a mark of special favour. Psalm 41:9 stands behind the scene: “one who ate of my bread has lifted the heel against me” (John 13:18).
In John's Gospel light and darkness are always more than time of day (John 1:5; 3:19; 8:12). Nicodemus came by night and moved towards the light; Judas goes out into the night.
The Romans called the third watch of the night, from midnight to three, “cockcrow” (Mark 13:35). By dawn Peter will have denied his Lord.
fathers: And it was night: and he who went out was himself the night. He went out from the light of the world into darkness, because he chose to love darkness rather than light.
Peter wept, and I do not read what he said; I read that he wept. Tears wash away the sin which the voice is ashamed to confess. Peter wept bitterly so that he might wash away his fault with tears.
outline: Ask: when have you failed someone you loved, and what did you do next?
The Servant's mission and his sense of failure.
Point 2 · A light to the nations
“I will give you as a light to the nations.”
live: Offer to God one work that seems to have been in vain, and leave the result to him.
Bring to confession this week the sin you are most tempted to hide in the night.
Pray for someone who has left
Pray by name for one person who has left the Church or the faith, that they may come back like Peter.
2027-03-23.prayer: Lord Jesus, you were called from the womb to be a light to the nations, and in the night of betrayal you went on loving to the end. When we fail you, do not let us go out into the night like Judas, but look at us as you looked at Peter, so that we may weep, return and follow you. Make your salvation reach to the ends of the earth. Amen.
altar: In the Upper Room Jesus gave a morsel even to the one who would betray him. At the altar he gives himself to sinners again; let us receive him not with Judas's heart but with Peter's repentant love.

quick: The Servant is called from the womb and made a light to the nations.
Judas takes the morsel and goes out: and it was night.
Peter promises to die for Jesus and will deny him, but he will weep and return.
2027-03-23.action: Go to confession this week, before the Triduum begins.
2027-03-23.question: After I fail, do I go out into the night like Judas, or turn back with tears like Peter?

family.explain: Peter said to Jesus: I will die for you! But Jesus knew that Peter would be afraid and would say three times that he did not know him. Later Peter was very sorry and cried, and Jesus forgave him. Jesus always forgives us when we come back.
family.intention: We pray for everyone who is sad because of their sins, that they may come back to Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone I need to say sorry to today?”

illus: A young man from a coastal parish near Kollam stopped going to church after a public quarrel and some foolish words he was ashamed of. For three years he avoided the priest. One Holy Week his little sister asked him to take her to the penitential service. He stood at the back. When the priest read “Peter went out and wept bitterly,” he found himself in the confession line. He said later: I thought I was Judas. That night I found out I was allowed to be Peter.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, light of the nations, in the night of betrayal you kept on loving. Look on us as you looked on Peter. Amen.
share: I have labored in vain (Isaiah 49:4). Where do I feel my efforts have come to nothing?
And it was night (John 13:30). Where is there night in my heart?
I will lay down my life for you (John 13:37). Do I trust my own strength more than his grace?
pm.resp: I will sing of your salvation.
interc: For missionaries who carry the light of Christ to the ends of the earth.
For those who have betrayed the trust of others, that they may not despair.
For all who have left the faith, that they may return like Peter.
For priests hearing confessions this Holy Week.
For our group, that we may follow Jesus faithfully this week.
pm.close: Father, you made your Servant a light to the nations. Keep us in his light, and let no one be lost in the night. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, in today's first reading the Servant speaks: the LORD called me before I was born, while I was in my mother's womb he named me (Isaiah 49:1). And then he admits: I have labored in vain, I have spent my strength for nothing (Isaiah 49:4). But God answers: it is too small a thing to restore only Israel; I will give you as a light to the nations, that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth (Isaiah 49:6).

In the Upper Room this light seems to be going out. Jesus is troubled in spirit and says: one of you will betray me. He gives a piece of bread, a sign of friendship, to Judas. Judas takes it and goes out. And it was night (John 13:30).

Then Peter says: I will lay down my life for you. Jesus answers: before the cock crows, you will have denied me three times (John 13:38). Two apostles fail him that night. Judas despairs; Peter weeps and returns. The difference is not that Peter's sin was small, but that Peter trusted the mercy of Jesus.

This Holy Week, do not go out into the night. Whatever you have done, come back to the light. Go to confession. Let Jesus look at you as he looked at Peter. From that weak, forgiven fisherman the light of Christ reached to the end of the earth, and it reaches you today. Amen.
kids: Children, Peter said he would never leave Jesus, but he got scared and said he did not know him. Then he was very sorry and cried, and Jesus forgave him and made him the leader of the apostles! When we do wrong, let us say sorry quickly and come back to Jesus.

intro: Theme: “I will give you as a light to the nations.”
The Servant called from the womb, the night of Judas and the tears of Peter.

q: The LORD called me before I was born, while I was in my mother's womb he named me.
and it is no longer I who live, but it is Christ who lives in me. And the life I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me.
points.apply: Thank God tonight for your own call, and offer him one work that seems to have failed.

sub: Salvation to the end of the earth.
q: I will give you as a light to the nations, that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth.
For so the Lord has commanded us, saying, ‘I have set you to be a light for the Gentiles, so that you may bring salvation to the ends of the earth.’
points.apply: Pray and give something this week for the missions.

sub: The night of a heart that refuses the light.
q: Even my bosom friend in whom I trusted, who ate of my bread, has lifted the heel against me.
So, after receiving the piece of bread, he immediately went out. And it was night.
points.apply: Bring into the light of confession the sin you most want to hide.

sub: I will lay down my life.
The look of Jesus and the way back.
q: For you, O Lord, are my hope, my trust, O LORD, from my youth.

“Simon, Simon, listen! Satan has demanded to sift all of you like wheat, but I have prayed for you that your own faith may not fail; and you, when once you have turned back, strengthen your brothers.”
points.apply: Make your confession before the Triduum, and trust his mercy more than your strength.

concl: The Servant's apparent failure becomes the light of the world.
Judas and Peter both fail; mercy is refused by one and received by the other.
2027-03-23.resolve: Choose Peter's tears, not Judas's night: go to confession before Holy Thursday.
